exact_statement: Let g be any Boolean function on a finite uniform cube, m=ghat(empty)^2. Let D be a nonnegative subprobability with D(empty)=m and finite c=CE(P_g,D). Supply normalized S,Q with S>=D, Q(empty)>=m, and Q(T)>=gamma D(T) for every nonempty T, 0<gamma<=1. For every finite adaptive tree querying fresh physical coordinates per path, at any chosen subset of stopping leaves reset to the direct marginal of S with ONE final vacuum calibration to the actual child mean-square, using the explicit empty point law for constant children; all other leaves retain the full inherited direct marginal of Q. Expected spectral erasure debits plus all complete terminal cross entropies are at most c+(1-m^2)log2(1/gamma). More sharply the excess is at most log2(1/gamma) times the sum over retained leaves of physical reach times [(1-m)+m Var(g_leaf)]. An arbitrary continuation below a fresh frontier leaf, with further calibrations of the CURRENT inherited reference, is paid by the complete-reference chain and nonpositive calibration costs; retained old frontier leaves admit no-reset continuation. This supplies no influence-priced reference, no likelihood floor for arbitrary incoming profiles, and no repeated return to the ORIGINAL source marginal after intervening calibrations. Entropy units bits.
hypotheses: Uniform finite Boolean physical cube; fresh physical coordinates per path; arbitrary finite adaptive stopping
D is only an auxiliary subprobability, never an actual supplied reference
Normalized S,Q, supplied occupied-support likelihood floor and finite source comparison cost
All final references include their full vacuum, ghosts and normalizers; each first reset uses one final calibration from the original S marginal; later calibrations use the CURRENT reference

exact_statement: For a complete normalized reference R, vacuum calibration C_p(R), and spectral coordinate deletion M preserving the empty atom, C_q(M C_p(R))=C_q(M R) whenever the stated calibrations have finite actual cross entropy on a Boolean physical history. For nonconstant histories alpha=(1-p)/(1-R(empty))>0 and 1-(M C_p(R))(empty)=alpha[1-(M R)(empty)], so the second calibration cancels alpha exactly on every nonempty atom; constant histories use the explicit empty point law. Consequently, for ANY finite uniform Boolean g, m=E[g]^2, finite-cost subprobability D with D(empty)=m, normalized S>=D and normalized Q with Q(empty)>=m and Q(T)>=gamma D(T) on nonempty atoms,0<gamma<=1,c=CE(P_g,D), every finite adaptive physical tree with arbitrary nested resets to C_(E[g_h]^2)(M_h S), keeping all other current references and complete terminals, has total expected erasures plus final complete CE at most c+(1-m^2)log2(1/gamma). The sharper surcharge charges only final branches with no source reset on their path, by log2(1/gamma) times sum w[(1-m)+m Var(g_leaf)]. After the first source reset, each ORIGINAL-source calibrated return equals CURRENT-reference calibration and costs minus its actual binary vacuum KL, so no original bank is renewed. For a genuinely different normalized nonempty profile the exact remaining reset cost is -D_Ber(q||v)+(1-q)[D(P_nonempty||R_new)-D(P_nonempty||R_old)], with finite-CE endpoint conventions. This constructs no influence-priced root reference or universal likelihood floor and is not full FEI.
hypotheses: Finite uniform Boolean cube; fresh physical coordinates, possibly outcome-adaptive finite stopping and reset policies
All actual references normalized and finite on occupied spectra; D is an auxiliary subprobability only
Original source reference S is fixed; targets are its direct path marginals followed by calibration to the actual squared mean
Both complete terminal costs and all executed erasure debits remain; no unrelated channel, integer-code or positive-only reset fee is inferred
Nonconstant denominators positive by finite CE; constant descendants use explicit empty point laws
